review.note:
Re-verification of SLICE-46 / FEAT-033 after the blocker fixup, commit 96722039, scope `git diff ec0e0de8..96722039`.

The fixup (one commit on top of ae411639) is exactly the one line expected: `src/tests/bootstrap-context.test.mts:10` now resolves `HOOKS_JSON` to `path.join(REPO_ROOT, "hooks", "hooks.json")`, matching the constant rename already done in `src/scripts/validate-repo-boundary.mts`. Nothing else in the diff changed — `git diff ec0e0de8..96722039 --stat` shows the same 10 files from my prior review plus this single-line edit to `bootstrap-context.test.mts`.

I reproduced the fix myself rather than taking the commit message on faith: `bun test src/tests/bootstrap-context.test.mts` -> 5 pass, 0 fail (previously 4 pass, 1 fail with ENOENT on the dead path). The lead separately ran the full root suite (`bun run test`) at 3448 pass, 7 skip, 0 fail across 337 files, which covers blocking CI gate 41 end to end.

All prior findings from my first pass (hooks relocation correctness, manifest hygiene, ci-gates.md gate count/order, README outside the metrics-band markers, CHANGELOG entry, docs/memory.md durable-fact framing, AC-checkmark honesty, touches-files.test.mts fixtures being inert) still hold — nothing in this fixup touches any of that surface.

Decision: approved. The one blocking regression from my prior review is fixed and verified live; no new issues found in the fixup itself.

validation.note:
SLICE-46 (FEAT-033) live validation: Claude Code plugin hook discovery at `hooks/hooks.json` confirmed empirically, and the AC-1/AC-3 gates re-confirmed on live state.

Scenario 1 (live discovery, AC-2 underlying mechanism): staged a minimal plugin copy (`.claude-plugin/` + `hooks/` only) with one extra SessionStart command appended to `hooks/hooks.json` that writes a marker file into `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`. Ran `claude -p --plugin-dir <plugin> --max-budget-usd 0.5 --model haiku "Reply with exactly: OK"` against a fresh one-commit consumer repo twice: once with the shipped layout (`hooks/hooks.json`), once with a control layout reproducing the pre-fix location (`.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json`, with `hooks/hooks.json` absent). The marker file appeared only in the shipped-layout run and was absent in the control run, isolating plugin-root path as the variable that determines discovery. `.claude/logs/events.jsonl` appeared in both runs and is explicitly not evidence by itself (the host's separately-installed crew 0.67.0 plugin also writes it).

Scenario 2 (AC-1/AC-3 gates): `bun test src/tests/install/hooks-discovery.test.mts` -> 4 pass, 0 fail (rc=0), matching the slice's recorded evidence exactly. `bun src/scripts/validate-repo-boundary.mts` -> `validate-repo-boundary: OK` (rc=0), also matching. Read the test file (not modified, not re-run against an altered tree): the first test ("hooks/hooks.json exists at the plugin root") asserts exists(REPO_ROOT/hooks/hooks.json) === true and would fail directly if the file were absent; the fourth test ("hooks/hooks.json parses as JSON...") would also fail (via an uncaught ENOENT from readFile) since it reads the same path. Both are driven from the live repo tree via import.meta.url-derived REPO_ROOT, not a copy, so no modification to the repo was needed or performed to make this determination.

No file under C:\work\mega\devcrew was modified. All staged/control plugin copies and the fresh consumer repo live under the scratch directory only.
